Let myself go in the last year and hopped back on the saddle a couple weeks ago. >21
>5'10
>190lbs
>~23%bf
>sedentary besides my workouts

This has all become pretty manageable because Im actually motivated this time around and have gone through losing weight a few times before. I have one main concern though

I did keto for about 6 months when I was at my most slim a few years ago. It was the most effective thing I found for losing weight. but it definitely changed how I view food. Even since falling off with my exercise / diet, I notice the foods I crave are still mostly fatty ones. My current macros are a result of me eating the foods I find enjoyable and sustainable so I dont break my diet, cop out, and eat awful stuff

title: Self experiment: NoFap lowers Test and Est
comment:
So, as I told you, I did the test and est level check after ~60 days of nofap (1 pollution at night around the mid-way point, but this is a huge achievement for me anyway, so it won't get any better than that). Outcome:

>BOTH TESTO (from 3.41 to 2.2) and ESTRO (from abnormal high 43k to high 33k) lowered.

Some additional info to put this into perspective
>I have Hashimoto's Disease (autoimune hypothyroid) which was misdiagnosed for a long time
>Beginning middle age, but had Hashimoto's and low test for decades, so it's not a purely age-related thing
>I am 6'1 and ~185 lbs, down from ~310 via some esoteric diet according to Chinese and European trad medicine (spoiler: It's mostly meat and grains)
>BMI is high normal
>I train kickboxing and ballistic exercises like jumping and sprinting and throwing 3x a week for 1.5-2 hours
>Additionally I take a walk around for 30-60 min every day
>My calories are low (1300-1800/day), so is fat (under 30% of daily calories), in 1.5 to 2 meals per day, this is well under my BMR
>Protein intake is low-ish by US standard (most comes from half a pound of meat per day)
>When fat, calories and protein intake were higher, I was also low test
>I get out in the sun for at least 1 hour every day (skin type 1, blond, green eyes) for Vit D
>I have no idea why the IOdine levels are so high, I avoid iodine-rich food because of Hashimoto's

So, in my case, Nofap does NOT work to raise testosterone. The opposite actually. You could argue the calories are too low, or the fat, or the protein, all of which are valid concerns, so one could say Nofap isn't strong enough to outperform any of those things. 

So there you have it. Any thoughts or questions?

PS: Please notice the different lab units for Eurofags before you flip out.

>having a great day at the gym, hit multiple PRs including 200 pound dumbbell rows for 6 
>decide to do a drop set of dumbbell curls after the rows
> of course start heavy-ish and work my way down to baby weight
>when I get down to baby weights I notice this one guy who seems to be around my age shirtless posing In front of the mirrors right in front of the dumbbells, with I think was his tripod but it might’ve been someone else’s.
>have to walk around him to get the baby weight dumbbells, I was pretty close to him in the process to be fair. 
>he says something to me and I have to take my earbuds out to hear him 
>”excuse me would have been a nice word”
>I respond “I’m locked in my dude I’m really not paying attention like that” 
>he basically shuts the exchange down and says something along the lines of “you’re good bro” and I just continue doing what I was doing.

Anons, was my response appropriate and should I have took it as disrespect? I’m kind of torn because one part of me is like “I just dumbbells rowed well above your body weight for reps do not play with me right now I do not care about your weak ass poses for TikTok while you hog up space in front of the dumbbells”

And another part of me was like “maybe he didn’t even mean it disrespectfully and was just trying to tell me he wasn’t trying to stand in my way” 

I have a hard time interpreting things as disrespectful or not so things like this really bother me. Did I have the right response and was this even disrespectful? Do I have Better things to do than worry about what some random at the gym says to me?

title: Cracked the Code for ∞ Gainz
comment:
>Full-body style workout
>Spread 1 or 2 exercises throughout the day
>Low volume, spending 5 to 10 minutes per exercise, only doing really 1 to 2 sets 1 to 5 RIR.
>Early morning: Pullups, dips 
>Morning: Overhead pressing
>Mid-Morning: Do some heavy squatting variation
>Noon: More dips or benching
>Afternoon: Rows, maybe do some carries
>Mid-Afternoon: Sprints or RDLs
>Evening: Curls and overhead extensions
>Mid Evening: Conditioning, play around at park
>Before bed: Bodyweight squats, pushups, pullups

This is kind of an example of just what you could do, this depends on how you feel and general energy level. If you feel good, do a bit more or throw in an extra exercise. If you feel a bit tired or sore, take it easy and either do something or easier or a different exercise all together. Nothing it set in stone and there isn't a big script to follow.

You can't tell me you won't get bigger arms by doing a curl variation every day or bigger legs by doing some squats every day, all for lower volume and not to the point of suicide.

title: For the poorfags
comment:
Feel free to screenshot
>diet
For anons who want to use a diet of 190g of protein and 2100kcal per day for only $125 a month while covering all micro needs, you have the following daily ingredients
>6 cups of whole milk
>2 scoops of whey protein
>2 cups cooked lentils/split peas
>1 cup cooked beans
>1 can of sardines
>1/4 head of cabbage
>2 large carrots
>salt to taste
You can also add cheap things like pepper, garlic, lemon, various spices and herbs, seasonal fruits and vegetables too to keep yourself from going crazy. Make a variety of dishes with the legumes, fish, and vegetables to further keep yourself sane. Added ingredients should only bring up the total for the month to $150 at most. Femanons can cut down on all the higher calorie items like whole milk and split peas since they don't need as much for protein and calories each day. Calories on the cheap can always be gotten with things like bread, rice, peanuts/peanut butter, oil, and so on
>exercise
Since the gym will be an iffy expense if you don't have something like a Planet Fitness or another really cheap option available, you can always use rings. It's a $20 expense that you can use for the rest of your life and gives you the ability to work the entire upper body. You can get very far with pullups, ring rows, dips, and pushup variations. You can even use the rings for isolation work like ring curls so you can get bigger arms. If you absolutely want to lift weights, since you can't afford to buy any normal weights, you can use rope as your handle. You can tie the rope onto something reasonably heavy and use it for things like lateral raises, curls, overhead extensions, and more. You can improvise weights by filling old containers with sand, water, concrete (be sure to reinforce it), all kinds of things to create a weight set for the rope. You can also go to the junkyard and find metal objects and reuse them as lifting equipment. That's how a lot of oldschool equipment was born.

title: Insane gains doing a seemingly retarded program for 3 years

I destroyed my back in a motorcycle accident and for years after i couldn't do most exercises due to having to wait between surgery and waiting for rods to be removed etc, this covered 4 years where I couldn't squat, deadlift, almost any rowing, row free weight pressing. I was limited to lat pulldowns and machine rows for back, machine chest press and machine shoulder press both with no lockouts. Cable arm work. Leg isolation for leg days. 

Anyway I went from 260 at 38% bodyfat to 175 at 11% bodyfat over 4 years, both were done with dexa.

>Waist went from 49 to 34


Monday - chest and arms
>1. Machine chest press (no lockout) 4 sets

>2.Facing away cable curls 4 sets

>3. Cable overhead extensions (straight bar) 4 sets

>4. Forearm standing pushing down cable curls4 sets

>5. 20 minutes on eliptical or stationary bike


Wednesday - Back and Shoulders
>1. Overhand lat pulldown (upper back not too wide a grip) 4 sets

>2. Machine row (Focus on lats) 4 sets

>3. Machine shoulder press (no lockout) 4 sets

>4.Cable lateral raises 4 sets

>5. 20 minutes on eliptical or stationary bike


Friday - Legs
>1. Leg press calf raises 4 sets

>2.Glute abduction machine 4 sets

>3. Leg extensions 4 sets

>4. Hamstring curls4 sets

>5. 20 minutes on eliptical or stationary bike

This board is obsessed with finding the easiest way of doing things and then working backwards to justify why its the best way to work out. 
>oh yeah, you definitely gotta bulk hard for most of the year if you wanna make gains. make sure to eat a lot of ice cream and have 4 large meals a day if you wanna make gains!
>oh yeah, PPL is definitely the ideal split. You definitely need 72-96 hours rest per muscle group between each work out session. Anything more than 2x a week frequency is overtraining!!!
>you dont wanna do heavy compounds bro, they're a waste of energy. Just hit isolations - that will maximise how much you can hit each muscle for your exhaustion quota. 
>cardio is for pussies bro, if you go for a run you're literally burning away your muscles.
>don't eat any vegetables man, they're all estrogenic and will give you aids.
The reality is that truly making it requires hard work, sacrifice, and discipline. You have to work out with high intensity AND high frequency, while having the self awareness to know you're not going to injure yourself. You have to work yourself to the point of discomfort every single session. You will have to work out at times when you don't feel like it. You have to get used to the feeling of hunger. You have to choose not to eat even when you want to. It's a cliche but nothing is more accurate than "no pain no gain". If you are not suffering in one way or another, you are not going to progress.

I'm averaging 0.5kg to 2.0kg of weight loss a week, but I don't track week to week anywhere. At my fatness as long as the scale number keeps going down it's good.

I was headed to being one of the landwhales, peaking (for a misuse of the word) at 105kg at 170cm.

Fitness isn't hard, but it takes effort. Most of the "work" is in the kitchen and your mentality of food and exercise. At this point, no matter how I feel - beyond injury - I exercise five days a week. It doesn't matter if I'm tired, feel a bit off, have a lot on my mind, slept lousy, or it's cold and snowing out; my feet move under me before my consciousness gets a chance to protest.

I eat less and better food, but somehow still feel like I'm pigging out. It's strange, but I'm consistently watching the weight fall away and I'm not hungry at all.

The biggest pain in the ass is I'm eventually going to have to replace every piece of clothing I own because they're all starting to look ridiculously large on me.

I still enjoy my tortilla chips & salsa, just not as much at once. I still eat cookies, hot cocoa and all the other "bad stuff" but no longer to gross excess.

I'm guessing I've got about eighteen months or so to go yet before I'm at the fitness level I want to maintain - but god-damn it I *WILL* be fitter at fifty than I was at thirty.
